policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'which were ready to die' reflects the base plural subject and ἀποθανεῖν; the RP second-person ἔμελλες with ἀποβάλλειν would mean that the addressee was about to cast away the remaining things.
ASV 'the things that remain' can render either the explicit substantival article τὰ or an English nominal expansion of the participle, so it does not securely distinguish the readings.
ASV has 'I will come as a thief' without 'upon thee' at this occurrence, excluding the RP addition ἐπί σε. The later 'upon thee' renders a separate base-text phrase after the second ἥξω.
ASV 'thou shalt not know' does not distinguish the aorist subjunctive γνῷς from the future γνώσῃ.
The readings differ only in Greek word order; ASV 'thou hast a few names' is a natural rendering of either.
ASV 'shall thus be arrayed' directly reflects the adverb οὕτως; the RP demonstrative οὗτος would require a nominal subject such as 'this one'.
ASV 'of David' does not distinguish the indeclinable name alone from an unrepresented Greek article before it.
ASV 'and that shutteth and none openeth' reflects the base καὶ κλείων construction, not the RP replacement 'it, except the one opening'.
ASV present 'openeth' reflects base ἀνοίγει rather than RP future ἀνοίξει.
ASV present 'I give' can render either contracted διδῶ or δίδωμι.
Within the ἵνα clause ASV 'to come and worship' does not securely distinguish future indicatives from aorist subjunctives.
English requires an explicit subject in 'I have loved thee', so ASV does not show whether emphatic Greek ἐγώ is present.
ASV relative clause 'which cometh down' can render either the participle καταβαίνουσα or finite καταβαίνει.
ASV 'the Amen' has an English article, but the surrounding Greek already contains an article for the title; it does not establish the additional article in the WH reading.
ASV's correlative 'neither hot nor cold' reflects base οὔτε; RP οὐ would give simple negation rather than the first member of the pair.
ASV begins the sentence 'Because thou sayest', directly reflecting base ὅτι; the RP omission lacks this causal conjunction.
ASV 'have need of nothing' reflects the genitive οὐδενός selected by χρείαν, rather than accusative οὐδέν.

The apparatus addition is anchored after the conjunction before 'knowest not'; ASV has no nominal expression there, so its wording supports the base without ὁ. The later 'the wretched one' renders the separate base-text article before ταλαίπωρος.
The readings differ only in the order of 'from me' and 'gold'; ASV's English order is not sufficient to select a Greek order.
ASV infinitival 'to anoint thine eyes' directly reflects base ἐγχρῖσαι rather than RP ἵνα with a subjunctive ('that thou mayest anoint').
ASV 'be zealous' does not distinguish the present imperative ζήλευε from the aorist imperative ζήλωσον.
ASV retains 'and he with me' after 'I ... with him', reflecting base καί; the WH/Treg omission would be asyndetic.
